title: Differential forms, orthonormal frames and Cartan methods
scope: Index-free exterior calculus and frame methods on a manifold: wedge products, p-forms and multivectors with their sheet-tube-cell pictures and pairings, the exterior derivative and dd = 0, closed and exact forms and the Poincare lemma, integration of forms over oriented chains, the boundary operator and the generalized Stokes theorem, volume forms, hypersurface forms and the Hodge star, Maxwell's equations and automatic conservation in form language; orthonormal frames, tetrads and vielbeins (including null tetrads and the static-observer frame) with frame components as observer measurements; and Cartan's calculus of vector-valued forms, connection 1-forms, the two structure equations, curvature 2-forms, the Cartan method for computing curvature and the Bianchi identity in forms. Coordinate volume elements and densities, noncoordinate bases, parallel-propagated frames and Lie derivatives are owned by neighbouring domains.

concepts.title: Orientation (handedness)
concepts.summary: An orientation is the sign attached to an ordered set of directions spanning an area or volume: swapping any two directions reverses it. Antisymmetric objects such as wedge products and volume forms measure oriented, signed sizes rather than absolute ones.
concepts.notes: Underlies the sign conventions of wedge products, volume forms, boundary orientation and flux integrals.

concepts.title: Wedge product
aliases: graded commutativity of the wedge product
concepts.summary: The wedge (exterior) product is the antisymmetrized tensor product of forms or of vectors; for 1-forms sigma wedge tau = sigma tensor tau - tau tensor sigma, so any 1-form wedged with itself vanishes. A p-form wedged with a q-form gives a (p+q)-form, and swapping the factors multiplies by (-1)^{pq}.

names: graded commutativity of the wedge product
components of a wedge of two 1-forms
graded commutativity of the wedge product

merged_from: graded commutativity of the wedge product
components of a wedge of two 1-forms
concepts.notes: Normalization differs between texts: Gifted Amateur uses no factor of 1/2 (u wedge v = u tensor v - v tensor u); others include 1/p!. Components of a wedge of two 1-forms are sigma_mu tau_nu - tau_mu sigma_nu, the 3D cross product arranged as a 2-form.

concepts.title: Bivector
concepts.summary: A bivector is an antisymmetric (2,0) tensor such as u wedge v; it represents the oriented plane element spanned by two vectors, and its components are the signed areas of that parallelogram projected onto the coordinate planes.
concepts.notes: The signed 2D area u^x v^y - v^x u^y = epsilon_ij u^i v^j is the entry point: positive when v is anticlockwise from u, sign flips on swapping.

concepts.title: Two-form
concepts.summary: A 2-form is an antisymmetric (0,2) tensor, written (1/2) B_{mu nu} omega^mu wedge omega^nu, with n(n-1)/2 independent components in n dimensions. It can be pictured as a lattice of oriented tubes where two stacks of 1-form sheets intersect; fed two vectors it returns the signed number of tubes threading their parallelogram.
concepts.notes: The factor 1/2 in the expansion compensates for each independent index pair appearing twice; explicit term-by-term expansions omit it. Example: a 3D fluid flux through a parallelogram is a 2-form whose components match the velocity vector (the seed of Hodge duality).

concepts.title: Differential form (p-form)
concepts.summary: A differential p-form is a totally antisymmetric (0,p) tensor field: it takes p vectors, returns a number, and changes sign when any two inputs are swapped. Functions are 0-forms and covector fields are 1-forms; in n dimensions forms of degree above n vanish and there are n choose p independent basis p-forms.

names: vanishing of forms of degree above the dimension

merged_from: vanishing of forms of degree above the dimension
concepts.notes: Geometric ladder: 1-forms as sheets, 2-forms as tubes, 3-forms as cells. The name 1-form traces to Cartan. In 4D spacetime nothing beyond a 4-form survives.

concepts.title: Ordered index summation (vertical-bar indices)
concepts.summary: Indices enclosed in vertical bars, as in B_{|mu nu|}, are summed only over increasing orderings (mu < nu), so each independent basis form appears once and the 1/p! factor of a full sum is dropped. Mixing the two conventions is a common source of factor-of-two errors.
concepts.notes: Used heavily when reading Riemann components off curvature 2-forms, where components sometimes need reordering to match wedge order.

concepts.title: Multivector (p-vector)
concepts.summary: A p-vector is a totally antisymmetric (p,0) tensor built from wedge products of vectors; a simple p-vector u_1 wedge ... wedge u_p represents the oriented p-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by its factors. Bivectors, trivectors and 4-vectors are the cases p = 2, 3, 4.
concepts.notes: Serves as the infinitesimal domain element when forms are integrated.

concepts.title: Interior product
aliases: contraction of a vector into a form
concepts.summary: The interior product inserts a vector into the first slot of a p-form, leaving a (p-1)-form; for example, inserting u into sigma wedge tau gives sigma(u) tau - tau(u) sigma.
concepts.notes: Inserting a unit normal into the volume form gives the surface area form; inserting a basis vector gives the hypersurface 3-form.

concepts.title: Pairing of forms with multivectors
aliases: inner product of a p-form and a p-vector
pairing of a 2-form with a bivector
concepts.summary: A p-form and a p-vector combine into a number, normalized so a basis p-form paired with the matching basis p-vector gives 1; for a simple p-vector it equals the form evaluated on the constituent vectors, and geometrically it counts the form's sheets, tubes or cells inside the parallelepiped.

names: inner product of a p-form and a p-vector
evaluation identity for a 2-form on a wedge of vectors
tube counting interpretation of the pairing
inner product of a p-form and a p-vector
pairing of a 2-form with a bivector

merged_from: inner product of a p-form and a p-vector

tube counting interpretation of the pairing
concepts.notes: Key example: <F, c wedge d> = F(c, d). The component sum runs over ordered indices, which is 1/p! times the full contraction.

concepts.title: Exterior derivative
concepts.summary: The exterior derivative d is the unique linear map from p-forms to (p+1)-forms that gives the gradient 1-form df on functions, obeys the graded Leibniz rule d(alpha wedge beta) = d alpha wedge beta + (-1)^p alpha wedge d beta, and squares to zero. In components it differentiates each coefficient and wedges the new differential on the left, needing no connection or metric.

names: graded Leibniz rule for the exterior derivative
exterior versus covariant derivative on forms
exterior derivative of a 1-form from covariant derivatives
graded Leibniz rule for the exterior derivative

merged_from: graded Leibniz rule for the exterior derivative
exterior versus covariant derivative on forms
exterior derivative of a 1-form from covariant derivatives
concepts.notes: In 3D, d on 0-, 1- and 2-forms reproduces gradient, curl and divergence. For a torsion-free connection dA has components A_{gamma;beta} - A_{beta;gamma}, and index-free dA(u,v) = u[A(v)] - v[A(u)] - A([u,v]). Unlike nabla, d on p-forms (p >= 1) yields an antisymmetric form, not a general tensor.

concepts.title: Nilpotency of the exterior derivative (dd = 0)
concepts.summary: Applying the exterior derivative twice to any form gives zero, because mixed partial derivatives are symmetric while wedge products are antisymmetric. It packages curl grad = 0 and div curl = 0 and is the form-side counterpart of the boundary of a boundary vanishing.
concepts.notes: Holds for scalar-valued forms only; the exterior covariant derivative applied twice to a vector gives curvature instead of zero.

concepts.title: Closed and exact forms
aliases: path independence of integrals of exact 1-forms
concepts.summary: A form is closed if its exterior derivative vanishes and exact if it is the exterior derivative of another form; every exact form is closed because dd = 0. Integrals of an exact 1-form depend only on endpoints, like the work of a conservative force.

names: path independence of integrals of exact 1-forms

merged_from: path independence of integrals of exact 1-forms
concepts.notes: Standard counterexample: the vortex 1-form (-y dx + x dy)/r^2 on the punctured plane is closed but not exact; its integral once around the origin is 2 pi.

concepts.title: Poincare lemma
concepts.summary: On a contractible region (for instance a star-shaped one) every closed p-form with p >= 1 is exact. Where the region has holes, closed forms can fail to be exact, so exactness detects topology.
concepts.notes: For 1-forms simple connectivity suffices; the vortex form on the punctured plane shows what fails without it.

concepts.title: Integration of differential forms
aliases: integral as pairing of a form with tangent n-vectors
line integral as integral of a 1-form
flux integral as integral of a 2-form
concepts.summary: A p-form is the natural integrand over an oriented p-dimensional region: parametrize the region, pair the form with the wedge of the tangent vectors to get a function of the parameters, and integrate that ordinarily. Line integrals are integrals of 1-forms and flux integrals are integrals of 2-forms, and the Jacobian appears automatically from wedge antisymmetry.

names: integral as pairing of a form with tangent n-vectors
line integral as integral of a 1-form
flux integral as integral of a 2-form
integrating alpha = x^2 dy along a path

merged_from: integral as pairing of a form with tangent n-vectors
line integral as integral of a 1-form
flux integral as integral of a 2-form
concepts.notes: Geometric reading: a 1-form integral counts sheets crossed, a 2-form integral counts tubes pierced, a 3-form integral counts cells enclosed.

concepts.title: Chains, cycles and boundaries
concepts.summary: A p-chain is an oriented p-dimensional integration domain (formally an integer combination of oriented pieces), and the boundary operator sends it to its oriented (p-1)-dimensional edge. Chains with no boundary are cycles, and integration pairs p-forms with p-chains the way 1-forms pair with vectors.
concepts.notes: Whether every cycle is a boundary is a topological question, mirroring whether every closed form is exact.

concepts.title: The boundary of a boundary is zero
aliases: boundary of a boundary is zero
concepts.summary: Applying the boundary operator twice to any chain gives nothing: a closed surface bounding a volume has no edge, because every edge of its faces is traversed twice in opposite directions. Through Stokes theorem this is dual to dd = 0.

names: boundary of a boundary is zero
boundary of a boundary is zero
boundary of a boundary is zero

merged_from: boundary of a boundary is zero

concepts.title: Induced boundary orientation
aliases: outward normal orientation on spacetime boundaries
concepts.summary: If a region is oriented by an ordered set of tangent vectors whose first member points outward at the boundary, the boundary is oriented by the remaining vectors in order. In one dimension this gives plus at the end point and minus at the start; on a spacetime box the outward normal on the earlier time face points to the past.

names: outward normal orientation on spacetime boundaries

merged_from: outward normal orientation on spacetime boundaries
concepts.notes: Schutz makes the same choice for Gauss's law in four dimensions: dt on the later face, -dt on the earlier one.

concepts.title: Generalized Stokes theorem
aliases: duality between d and the boundary operator
concepts.summary: For a (p-1)-form omega and an oriented p-dimensional region V, the integral of d omega over V equals the integral of omega over the boundary of V with its induced orientation. It unifies the fundamental theorem of calculus, Green, Kelvin-Stokes and Gauss divergence theorems in one statement.

names: duality between d and the boundary operator

merged_from: duality between d and the boundary operator
concepts.notes: Read as an adjointness: d on forms is the partner of the boundary operator on chains. The telescoping-sum picture (interior contributions cancel, only the edge survives) is the standard motivation. d'Inverno states it in index form with the volume element of a subspace.

concepts.title: Volume form
concepts.summary: The volume form is the top-degree form equal to the wedge of an oriented orthonormal basis of 1-forms; in coordinates it is sqrt(|g|) dx^0 wedge ... wedge dx^3. Fed n vectors it returns the signed n-volume of the parallelepiped they span.

names: covariant constancy of the volume form

merged_from: covariant constancy of the volume form
concepts.notes: Examples: the plane area omega(u,v) is a 2x2 determinant; the 4-volume of a spacetime parallelepiped is a 4x4 determinant. With a metric-compatible connection the volume form is covariantly constant. Inserting a unit normal gives the surface-area 2-form. Components in an orthonormal frame are the Levi-Civita symbol with a chosen sign convention.

concepts.title: Hodge star operator
concepts.summary: The Hodge star is the metric-dependent linear map, built from the volume form, that sends a p-form to an (n-p)-form (or to an (n-p)-vector) with the same number of independent components and the same geometric content. Applying it twice returns the original up to the sign (-1)^{s+p(n-p)}, where s counts negative signs in the signature.

names: cross product as a Hodge dual
curl as a Hodge dual in curvilinear coordinates

merged_from: cross product as a Hodge dual
curl as a Hodge dual in curvilinear coordinates
concepts.notes: In Euclidean 3-space the cross product is the Hodge dual of a wedge, which is why a product of two vectors can be a vector only in three dimensions; the curl is star-d of the associated 1-form, bringing scale factors in curvilinear coordinates. In Minkowski space star-star = -1 on 2-forms. The inverse map needs the all-upper volume tensor, normalized so indices move with the metric.

concepts.title: Hypersurface 3-form
concepts.summary: In four dimensions, inserting a basis vector into the volume form gives the 3-form dSigma_mu, and inserting three edge vectors gives a 1-form; these represent oriented 3-volume elements of hypersurfaces. The spatial volume an observer with four-velocity u measures for a box with edges A, B, C is omega(u, A, B, C).
concepts.notes: Sign conventions matter: with Gifted Amateur's definitions spacelike hypersurfaces carry outward timelike normals and timelike hypersurfaces inward spacelike normals, which explains minus signs in spatial components.

concepts.title: Faraday 2-form
concepts.summary: The Faraday 2-form is the electromagnetic field tensor written as F = (1/2) F_{alpha beta} dx^alpha wedge dx^beta = E_i dx^i wedge dt + B_x dy wedge dz + B_y dz wedge dx + B_z dx wedge dy. It is the exterior derivative of the potential 1-form A, so it is automatically closed.
concepts.notes: Magnetic components can be drawn as circulation inside the tubes cut out by two families of coordinate sheets, replacing field-line arrows. Gauge changes A -> A + d(chi) leave F unchanged because dd = 0.

concepts.title: Maxwell 2-form (dual Faraday form)
concepts.summary: The Maxwell 2-form is the Hodge dual of the Faraday 2-form; its components are those of F with E replaced by -B and B by E. The sources couple to it, since the exterior derivative of F itself vanishes identically.
concepts.notes: Dualizing twice gives -F in Lorentzian signature, the duality rotation E -> -B, B -> E applied twice.

concepts.title: Current 3-form
concepts.summary: The current 3-form is the Hodge dual of the four-current, J^mu dSigma_mu; its purely spatial component is the charge density and its time-containing components carry the current density. Integrating it over a 3-surface gives the charge on or crossing that surface.

names: particle number in a box as a volume-form evaluation

merged_from: particle number in a box as a volume-form evaluation
concepts.notes: Same construction works for any conserved current, e.g. particle number: the number in a box with edges A, B, C is the volume form evaluated on (J, A, B, C).

concepts.title: Maxwell's equations in differential forms
concepts.summary: In form language electromagnetism is F = dA, hence dF = 0 (no monopoles and Faraday's law), together with d*F = *J (Gauss and Ampere-Maxwell laws), up to unit-dependent factors. The statement holds unchanged in any coordinates and in curved spacetime.
concepts.notes: dF = 0 is the component cyclic identity on F_{[mu nu, lambda]}.

concepts.title: Boundary-of-a-boundary principle (automatic conservation)
concepts.summary: When a field equation sets a source equal to the exterior derivative of a field form, conservation of the source is automatic: its flux through any closed 3-surface becomes an integral over the boundary of that surface, which is empty. For electromagnetism d*J = dd*F = 0 gives charge conservation; for gravity the same logic, via the contracted Bianchi identity, makes stress-energy conservation a consequence of the Einstein equation.

names: conservation of stress-energy in forms language

merged_from: conservation of stress-energy in forms language
concepts.notes: Wheeler's slogan, developed in Gifted Amateur ch43; the gravitational version (d*T = 0 with *G = 8 pi *T) appears only in exercises there.

concepts.title: Orthonormal frame (tetrad)
concepts.summary: An orthonormal frame is a set of basis vectors at each point, one timelike and three spacelike in spacetime, that are mutually orthogonal and unit-normalized so their inner products are eta. Components referred to it are what an observer carrying the frame measures, and frame indices are raised and lowered with eta rather than g.

names: observer 4-velocity as the time basis vector

merged_from: observer 4-velocity as the time basis vector
concepts.notes: Usually a noncoordinate basis: its connection coefficients need not vanish unless it is locally inertial. Coordinate bases are convenient for computation, orthonormal frames for measurement. Cartan's moving frame (repere mobile) views it as a field of frames that turns or boosts from point to point. Schutz meets the tetrad as the basis of an inertial frame; d'Inverno takes e_0 as the observer's four-velocity.

concepts.title: Vielbein
concepts.summary: The vielbein is the matrix (e_mu)^{a-hat} of components relating coordinate basis vectors to an orthonormal frame, together with its inverse; it satisfies g_{mu nu} = eta_{ab} (e_mu)^a (e_nu)^b. Finding a frame means finding a matrix that turns g into eta.

names: matrix form of the orthonormality condition
tetrads converting coordinate increments into ruler readings

merged_from: matrix form of the orthonormality condition
concepts.notes: The frame is fixed only up to a local Lorentz transformation: 16 vielbein components minus 10 metric components leaves 6 freedoms. The two matrices are inverses, so contracting one with the other gives a Kronecker delta.

concepts.title: Orthonormal coframe (basis 1-forms)
concepts.summary: The orthonormal coframe is the set of basis 1-forms omega^{a-hat} = (e_mu)^{a-hat} dx^mu dual to an orthonormal frame, in which the line element becomes a sum of signed squares, ds^2 = -(omega^0)^2 + (omega^1)^2 + (omega^2)^2 + (omega^3)^2. It is the starting point of Cartan's method.
concepts.notes: Special case already in Schutz ch04: an inertial observer can be specified by the 1-form -dt = g(U, .), a stack of simultaneity surfaces, instead of by U.

concepts.title: Frame components
concepts.summary: Frame components of a tensor are obtained by contracting each coordinate index with one vielbein (or inverse vielbein) factor, e.g. T_{a-hat b-hat} = T_{mu nu} (e_a-hat)^mu (e_b-hat)^nu. In an orthonormal frame they are the numbers an observer carrying the frame actually measures.

names: measurement as projection onto the observer's basis
transformation of 1-forms to an orthonormal frame
measured energy from the orthonormal frame

merged_from: transformation of 1-forms to an orthonormal frame
measured energy from the orthonormal frame
measurement as projection onto the observer's basis
concepts.notes: Raising a hatted time index flips sign because eta_00 = -1 (T^{0i} = -T_{0i}). Example: the measured energy of a photon at a static Schwarzschild observer is p^t times (1 - 2M/r)^{1/2}, the same as -p.u_obs. Coordinate components have no invariant meaning; frame components along physically chosen vectors do.

concepts.title: Orthonormal frame of a diagonal metric
concepts.summary: When the metric is diagonal, the orthonormal frame at rest in the coordinates is obtained by dividing each coordinate basis vector by sqrt|g_{mu mu}|; equivalently omega^{t-hat} = sqrt(-g_tt) dt, omega^{r-hat} = sqrt(g_rr) dr, and so on.

names: orthonormal frame for a diagonal metric
orthonormal frame for a diagonal metric
polar-plane coframe e1 = dr, e2 = r dphi

merged_from: orthonormal frame for a diagonal metric
concepts.notes: Examples: polar plane (dr, r d theta), 2-sphere (a d theta, a sin theta d phi), Robertson-Walker (1, a/sqrt(1-kr^2), a r, a r sin theta).

concepts.title: Orthonormal frame of a static observer
concepts.summary: A static observer holding fixed spatial coordinates carries the orthonormal frame obtained by normalizing the coordinate basis, with time leg along the observer's four-velocity. In Schwarzschild the vielbein components are (1 - 2M/r)^{1/2}, (1 - 2M/r)^{-1/2}, r and r sin theta, and the frame exists only outside r = 2M.
concepts.notes: Default frame whenever Gifted Amateur says "the orthonormal frame" without naming an observer; its metric is eta but its connection coefficients need not vanish, so it is not a local inertial frame. Used for relativistic stellar curvature, measured photon energies and tidal equations.

concepts.title: Frame formalism and the frame metric
concepts.summary: In the frame (tetrad) formalism tensors are described by their components along any four linearly independent vector fields rather than coordinate basis vectors; the inner products of the frame vectors form the frame metric g_ij, which raises and lowers frame indices and rebuilds g_ab = g_ij e^i_a e^j_b.

names: frame of reference versus coordinate system

merged_from: frame of reference versus coordinate system
concepts.notes: Orthonormal frames are the case g_ij = eta_ij; null tetrads give a constant off-diagonal frame metric.

concepts.title: Null tetrad
concepts.summary: A null tetrad consists of two real future-pointing null vectors l and n with l.n normalized to one, and a complex conjugate pair m, m-bar orthogonal to both with m.m-bar normalized; all four legs are null. It is built from an orthonormal frame as (T +/- X)/sqrt2 and (Y +/- iZ)/sqrt2.
concepts.notes: Signs of the normalizations depend on signature (d'Inverno uses +---). Simpler warm-up: Schutz's 2D null basis tied to u = t - x, v = t + x has off-diagonal metric components. Spin coefficients and Petrov types built on it belong to gravitational waves.

concepts.title: Vector-valued differential form
concepts.summary: A vector-valued 1-form eats a vector and returns a vector instead of a number; nabla v and de_mu are examples, and componentwise it is a sum of basis vectors tensored with 1-forms. Higher-degree versions, such as the curvature operator, are vector- or bivector-valued p-forms.
concepts.notes: Unlike a general (1,1) tensor, objects like nabla v depend on the connection for their construction. Cartan's displacement dP = e_mu tensor omega^mu is the identity vector-valued 1-form.

concepts.title: Exterior covariant derivative
concepts.summary: The exterior covariant derivative extends d to vector- and tensor-valued forms using the connection: for a vector field, dv is the vector-valued 1-form whose value on u is nabla_u v, computed by the product rule dv = e_mu tensor (dv^mu + omega^mu_nu v^nu).

names: exterior covariant derivative of a vector field
exterior derivative of a basis bivector
exterior derivative of a vector-valued 1-form on a bivector

merged_from: exterior covariant derivative of a vector field
exterior derivative of a basis bivector
exterior derivative of a vector-valued 1-form on a bivector
concepts.notes: Index-free formula for a tensor-valued 1-form S: <dS, u wedge v> = nabla_u <S,v> - nabla_v <S,u> - <S,[u,v]>. Example: d(e_mu wedge e_nu) = omega^alpha_mu e_alpha wedge e_nu + omega^beta_nu e_mu wedge e_beta.

concepts.title: Connection 1-forms
concepts.summary: The connection 1-forms omega^nu_mu record how basis vectors turn as one moves: de_mu = omega^nu_mu tensor e_nu, so omega^nu_mu(e_alpha) = Gamma^nu_{alpha mu}. In an orthonormal frame they act like infinitesimal rotation and boost generators of the frame.
concepts.notes: Gifted Amateur puts the differentiation index first on Gamma; check ordering when comparing texts.

concepts.title: Metric compatibility of connection 1-forms
aliases: antisymmetry of connection forms in an orthonormal frame
Lorentzian sign rule for hatted time indices
concepts.summary: Metric compatibility in form language reads dg_{mu nu} = omega_{mu nu} + omega_{nu mu}; in an orthonormal frame the metric is constant, so omega_{a b} = -omega_{b a}. With a Lorentzian eta this means spatial pairs are antisymmetric (omega^i_j = -omega^j_i) while time-space pairs are symmetric (omega^t_i = +omega^i_t).

names: Lorentzian sign rule for hatted time indices
antisymmetry of connection forms in an orthonormal frame

merged_from: antisymmetry of connection forms in an orthonormal frame
Lorentzian sign rule for hatted time indices
concepts.notes: In Cartan calculations this supplies the partner of each connection form for free; the induced antisymmetry carries over to the lowered curvature 2-forms.

concepts.title: Cartan's first structure equation
concepts.summary: For a torsion-free connection the coframe satisfies d omega^mu = -omega^mu_nu wedge omega^nu. Together with the antisymmetry of the orthonormal connection forms it determines the connection 1-forms, often by inspection.

names: displacement of a point as identity tensor

merged_from: displacement of a point as identity tensor
concepts.notes: Gifted Amateur derives it from d^2 P = 0 applied to Cartan's displacement dP = e_mu tensor omega^mu. With torsion the right-hand side gains the torsion 2-form.

concepts.title: Curvature as the second exterior covariant derivative
concepts.summary: Applying the exterior covariant derivative twice to a vector field does not give zero: all derivatives of the field cancel and what remains is a curvature operator acting on the vector, d^2 v = e_mu tensor R^mu_nu v^nu. A connection is flat exactly when d^2 v = 0 for every v.

names: curvature as the second exterior covariant derivative

merged_from: curvature as the second exterior covariant derivative
concepts.notes: The curvature operator can be written as a bivector-valued 2-form, (1/4)(e_mu wedge e_nu) R^{mu nu}_{alpha beta} omega^alpha wedge omega^beta; evaluated on u wedge v it gives the Riemann operator [nabla_u, nabla_v] - nabla_[u,v].

concepts.title: Curvature 2-form
concepts.summary: The curvature 2-forms R^mu_nu package the Riemann tensor by its antisymmetric last index pair: R^mu_nu = (1/2) R^mu_{nu alpha beta} omega^alpha wedge omega^beta, one 2-form per pair of frame indices. They are the gravitational analogue of the Faraday 2-form.

concepts.title: Cartan's second structure equation
aliases: R = d omega + omega wedge omega
concepts.summary: Cartan's second structure equation computes curvature from the connection forms: R^mu_nu = d omega^mu_nu + omega^mu_alpha wedge omega^alpha_nu. It is the form-language version of the Riemann formula built from derivatives and products of Christoffel symbols.
concepts.notes: Regarding Gamma_mu as matrices, the Riemann components form d_mu Gamma_nu - d_nu Gamma_mu + [Gamma_mu, Gamma_nu], the coordinate analogue.

concepts.title: Cartan's method for computing curvature
concepts.summary: Cartan's method finds the Riemann tensor without Christoffel symbols: choose an orthonormal coframe, compute its exterior derivatives, read off the connection 1-forms from the first structure equation and antisymmetry, build curvature 2-forms from d omega + omega wedge omega, and read Riemann components from their expansion, converting to coordinates with the vielbein if needed.

names: Cartan coframes on plane and sphere
surface of revolution with Cartan equations

concepts.notes: Worked cases: 2-sphere (frame value 1/a^2), polar plane (zero curvature despite nonzero connection forms), surfaces of revolution ds^2 = du^2 + f^2 dphi^2 giving R^1_2 = -(f''/f) e^1 wedge e^2, Schwarzschild interior, expanding universe, Kaluza-Klein reduction.

concepts.title: Bianchi identity in Cartan form
aliases: Cartan form of the Bianchi identity
concepts.summary: Differentiating the second structure equation and substituting it back gives dR^mu_nu = R^mu_alpha wedge omega^alpha_nu - omega^mu_alpha wedge R^alpha_nu; equivalently the exterior covariant derivative of the curvature 2-form vanishes. It is the forms version of the differential Bianchi identity.
